description: The staircase leg of M_n is closed form: V(delta_k) = A*k - B - F(n) up to a remainder decaying at the derived rate q0^4 per unit k, where A = sum_j eps(2j-1), B = sum_j (j-1)eps(2j-1). Follows from betaSide_eq_hookSum (the objective is cell-local in the hook length) plus the staircase hook multiset '2j-1 with multiplicity k+1-j'. Because k + 1/2 = sqrt(2n + 1/4) exactly at triangular n, the result is an IDENTITY rather than an asymptotic: M_n = A*sqrt(2n + 1/4) - A/2 - B - C + e_n + two exponentially small remainders, together 5.1e-16 at n = 3916. The entire gap to a closed asymptotic is the single sequence e_n; kappa = -A/2 - B - C + e_inf.

lean.role: makes the objective a sum over cells of a function of the hook length

checks.name: S1 hook length 2j-1 occurs exactly k+1-j times, and no even hook length occurs
checks.detail: 40/40 staircases k = 1..40 match the predicted multiset exactly, as integer counts — this is the whole input the closed form needs

checks.name: S2 sum_j (k+1-j)(2j-1) = k(k+1)(2k+1)/6 = H_min at n = T_k
checks.detail: 40/40 exact as integers, k = 1..40 — H_min is established independently (square-pyramidal closed form, hmin_closed_form_and_rev_sublinearity_probe), so this is a cross-check on S1 that does not reuse the enumeration

checks.name: S3 the SERIES form reproduces the committed staircase value at every n
checks.detail: 11/11 agree to 1e-12 — #7294 computed V_staircase from a beta-set through a pair sum; this computes it from a hook multiset with no beta anywhere, so the agreement is a check on betaSide_eq_hookSum as much as on the multiset

checks.name: S4 the CLOSED form's remainder decays at the DERIVED rate q0^4 per unit k
checks.detail: |remainder| falls 0.1635 (k = 8) -> 5.118e-16 (k = 88), a factor of 3.195e+14; the per-k rate converges to 1.517953249 against the predicted q0^4 = 1.51795325 (relative 6.76e-10).  The rate is derived from the leading omitted term eps(2k+3), so this tests the FORM of the remainder, not just its size

checks.name: S5 with the excess gap (iii) removed, the residual is (i) + (ii) alone and collapses
checks.detail: |residual - (iii)| falls 0.1658 (n = 36) -> 5.114e-16 (n = 3916) — so the decomposition M_n = A*sqrt(2n+1/4) - A/2 - B - C + e_n is EXACT at triangular n up to two exponentially small terms, and the entire gap to an asymptotic law is the single sequence e_n

checks.name: S5b the sqrt(2n+1/4) form is the exact one; plain sqrt(2n) costs an extra A/(8 sqrt(2n))
checks.detail: at n = 3916: residual 5.114e-16 exact-k against 0.00509 for plain sqrt(2n) — the difference is A(sqrt(2n+1/4) - sqrt(2n)) ~ A/(8 sqrt(2n)) = 0.0050896, which is why the constant term is only well-defined once the sqrt is written exactly

checks.name: S5c three of kappa's four pieces are explicit convergent series; only e_inf is measured
checks.detail: A = 3.60337772572, B = 5.18936914406, C = 6.17140572008 are sums of eps over arithmetic progressions and converge like q0^(-2m); e_inf = 2.43929480827 comes from a heuristic search at a single n and is the one open number — it is NOT proved to be a limit

verdict: V(staircase) = A*k - B - F(n), verified against all 11 committed points of #7294, with a remainder decaying at the derived rate q0^4 per unit k. At triangular n this is an IDENTITY, M_n = A*sqrt(2n + 1/4) - A/2 - B - C + e_n + (i) + (ii), with (i)+(ii) = 5.1e-16 at n = 3916; the plain sqrt(2n) form is NOT equivalent, it carries an extra A/(8 sqrt(2n)) = 0.0051 there. The open problem is now the single sequence e_n / its limit e_inf. M_n remains a lower bound -- the baseline is exact, the search is not.
